headings.title: SMTO-SKL-0070 — SMTO can only change an email that is still a draft

html:
SMTO-SKL-0070 — SMTO can only change an email that is still a draft

GUID: e52ea067-0ff2-5b08-8ae3-a118448bfbb8
Slug: microsoft365-draft-required
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • You asked SMTO to edit, delete or change attachments on an email draft, but that email is no longer a draft (for example, it was already sent). SMTO checked first and changed nothing.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Outlook with the same Microsoft account and look in the Drafts folder for the email you meant to change. If it isn't there, it was probably already sent, and a sent email can't be edited.
  2. If the draft is there, ask SMTO to find it in your Drafts folder by its subject and then make your change. SMTO was pointing at a different email; searching Drafts gives it the right one.
  3. If the email was already sent, ask SMTO to create a new draft with your changes instead. A new draft can be edited and reviewed before you send it.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the draft was updated, and you see the change in your Outlook Drafts folder.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO's Microsoft 365 setup. Don't ask SMTO to change a sent email; Outlook doesn't allow that.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Microsoft 365 draft operation (mail_update_draft, mail_delete_draft, mail_attachment_add or mail_attachment_delete) read the target message first and found isDraft was not true, so no write was sent.

What this means

  • A requested draft edit/delete first reads the message and isDraft is not true. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • A requested draft edit/delete first reads the message and isDraft is not true.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact message ID and the current isDraft value.

How to fix it

  • The pre-write GET of the message by its message_id returned isDraft false. Locate the intended draft with microsoft365.mail_search (folder_id of the Drafts folder) under the same account_ref and retry with that exact message_id, or create a new draft with microsoft365.mail_create_draft; do not edit sent or received messages through draft tools.
  • Choose the exact ID of a message whose isDraft value is true.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The operation targets the intended actual draft.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
